patch_description:
This evolution reduces the parameter count from 162 to 27 by implementing parameter sharing across the 6 block repetitions (3 uploads × 2 repeats). Instead of having independent parameters for each block instance, we reuse the same 27 parameter names across all blocks, which allows the optimizer to learn a single set of effective transformations that are applied repeatedly.

Additionally, we optimize the entanglement pattern:
- Keep RY rotations on all 9 qubits (9 params)
- Keep RZ pre-entanglement on all 9 qubits (9 params)
- Use a sparser CZ pattern: only the outer ring (8 edges) plus 4 center connections = 12 edges (same as before)
- Keep RZ post-entanglement on all 9 qubits (9 params)

The key insight is that parameter sharing leverages the data re-uploading structure: the feature map changes at each upload, so the same ansatz block can learn to respond differently to different feature inputs. This is more parameter-efficient and often leads to better generalization.

The reduced parameter count (27 vs 162) means:
- Fewer parameters to optimize (easier convergence)
- Lower circuit depth per block (since we're not changing the gate structure, just sharing params)
- Better parameter efficiency score
- Reduced risk of barren plateaus
